title: Unauthenticated calls can select the user context from the request body
reasoning: The route resolves the user id from authenticated context when present, but falls back to request.user_id when no authenticated identity exists, then uses that resolved id to generate the title with the shared container/session manager. For a network route with an auth trust boundary, this makes the authorization boundary optional at the handler level: a caller without identity can supply another user's id and potentially use that user's model/session configuration for title generation. The excerpt does not show a route-level dependency that rejects missing identity, so the handler itself does not enforce the boundary.
recommendation: Require an authenticated install identity for this route, or explicitly gate the unauthenticated local path behind a separate trusted transport/dependency. Do not use request.user_id as an authorization fallback for network requests; at most treat it as advisory and verify it matches the authenticated identity.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this route, and the excerpt has no evidence of a test covering missing authenticated identity or cross-user request.user_id spoofing.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route-level test for POST /api/semantic/title that verifies a request without authenticated identity is rejected, and a request whose body user_id differs from the authenticated identity cannot cause service.generate_title to receive the body user_id.
